clinician.final_diagnosis: Paget's disease of the nipple (histologically: invasive ductal carcinoma with epidermal involvement)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old man with strong family history of breast cancer (mother and two maternal aunts) presented with right breast pain, nipple retraction, and skin induration. Clinical examination revealed skin induration without palpable masses or bloody discharge. Punch biopsy of the right nipple-areolar complex was performed and demonstrated invasive ductal carcinoma with epidermal involvement that was estrogen receptor positive (ER+), progesterone receptor positive (PR+), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 positive (HER2+). Mammography revealed a high-density, irregularly shaped mass with spiculated margins in the retroareolar region with associated nipple and skin retraction. Breast ultrasound confirmed a 1.4 cm solid, hypoechoic, irregular mass at the retroareolar region. The patient underwent modified radical mastectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy that was positive for metastatic carcinoma, followed by full axillary dissection. Adjuvant chemoradiation therapy and estrogen blockade with tamoxifen were subsequently administered. The histopathologic findings of invasive ductal carcinoma with epidermal involvement are consistent with Paget's disease of the nipple, characterized by tumor cells distributed through the epidermis with pale cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli.
